verses.text: “My Son, anchor thy soul firmly upon God, and fear not man’s judgment, when conscience pronounceth thee pious and innocent.
verses.modernizedText: “My Son, anchor your soul firmly upon God, and do not fear man’s judgment when conscience pronounces you pious and innocent.

verses.text: It is good and blessed thus to suffer; nor will it be grievous to the heart which is humble, and which trusteth in God more than in itself.
verses.modernizedText: It is good and blessed to suffer thus; nor will it be grievous to the heart which is humble, and which trusts in God more than in itself.

verses.text: Many men have many opinions, and therefore little trust is to be placed in them.
verses.modernizedText: Many men have many opinions, and therefore little trust is to be placed in them.

verses.text: But moreover it is impossible to please all.
verses.modernizedText: But moreover it is impossible to please all.

verses.text: Although Paul studied to please all men in the Lord, and to become all things to all men,(1) yet nevertheless with him it was a very small thing that he should be judged by man’s judgment.”(2)
verses.modernizedText: Although Paul studied to please all men in the Lord, and to become all things to all men,(1) yet nevertheless with him it was a very small thing that he should be judged by man’s judgment.”(2)

verses.text: He laboured abundantly, as much as in him lay, for the building up and the salvation of others; but he could not avoid being sometimes judged and despised by others.
verses.modernizedText: He labored abundantly, as much as lay in him, for the building up and the salvation of others; but he could not avoid being sometimes judged and despised by others.

verses.text: Therefore he committed all to God, who knew all, and by patience and humility defended himself against evil speakers, or foolish and false thinkers, and those who accused him according to their pleasure.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore he committed all to God, who knew all, and by patience and humility defended himself against evil speakers, or foolish and false thinkers, and those who accused him according to their pleasure.

verses.text: Nevertheless, from time to time he replied, lest his silence should become a stumbling-block to those who were weak.
verses.modernizedText: Nevertheless, from time to time he replied, lest his silence should become a stumbling block to those who were weak.

verses.text: “Who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid of a man that shall die?
verses.modernizedText: “Who are you, that you should be afraid of a man who will die?

verses.text: To-day he is, and to-morrow his place is not found.
verses.modernizedText: Today he is, and tomorrow his place is not found.

verses.text: Fear God and thou shalt not quail before the terrors of men.
verses.modernizedText: Fear God and you will not quail before the terrors of men.

verses.text: What can any man do against thee by words or deeds?
verses.modernizedText: What can any man do against you by words or deeds?

verses.text: He hurteth himself more than thee, nor shall he escape the judgment of God, whosoever he may be.
verses.modernizedText: He hurts himself more than you, nor will he escape the judgment of God, whoever he may be.

verses.text: Have thou God before thine eyes, and do not contend with fretful words.
verses.modernizedText: Have God before your eyes, and do not contend with fretful words.

verses.text: And if for the present thou seem to give way, and to suffer confusion which thou hast not deserved, be not angry at this, nor by impatience diminish thy reward; but rather look up to Me in heaven, for I am able to deliver thee from all confusion and hurt, and to render to every man according to his works.”
verses.modernizedText: And if for the present you seem to give way, and to suffer confusion which you have not deserved, do not be angry at this, or by impatience diminish your reward; but rather look up to Me in heaven, for I am able to deliver you from all confusion and hurt, and to render to every man according to his works.”
